title: Sonora hosted API embeddings + rerank demo
summary: Redwood AE+SE gave a hosted API demo focusing on embeddings + reranking for Sonora's search product. Discussed integration path, latency vs cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2/KMS/VPC), and next steps for a short POC and benchmark run. Customer asked about data residency and custom model fine-tuning; Redwood suggested hosted embeddings plus rerank with canary rollout and sample benchmark to validate relevance improvement.
action_items: Lena Park: Share pricing deck and hosted vs dedicated decision matrix - due 2026-11-24
Marcus Chen: Run 5k-query rerank benchmark on sample dataset and share latency/cost spreadsheet - due 2026-11-27
Maya Lopez: Provide sample index export and ~5000 anonymized query logs for benchmark - due 2026-11-25
next_steps: AE to send pricing + security one-pager
SE to run benchmark and share results
Schedule POC kickoff (30-45 day) pending benchmark
Customer to confirm stakeholders and timeline by 2026-11-26
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-21
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (CTO, Sonora), Daniel Ruiz (Head of Search), Maya Lopez (Data Eng)
Link to deck: https://redwood.example.com/deck/sonora-demo

00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time. quick intros on our side i'm lena park, i'm the AE working with you all and marcus here is our solutions engineer.
00:08 Marcus Chen: hi all, i'll be doing most of the technical walkthrough today, focusing on embeddings and the rerank endpoint and how you'd integrate it into an existing search stack.
00:16 Priya Kumar: thanks lena, i'm priya, cto. curious about how this fits with our current elastic stack and what the cost looks like.
00:24 Daniel Ruiz: yeah hi i'm daniel, we run a fairly heavy search infra on elastic cloud, a lot of faceted search, and we want better relevance without huge latency hits.
00:33 Marcus Chen: great, that's exactly the common pattern we see. quick agenda: 1) show hosted embeddings API and embedding vectors, 2) rerank endpoint demo with candidate generation from elastic, 3) console and metric dashboards, 4) discuss security/compliance and POC next steps.
00:47 Lena Park: just flag, we're demoing hosted mode here — which gives fastest time to value. later we can talk dedicated/reserved capacity if you need predictable throughput.
00:58 Maya Lopez: quick question: we have data residency reqs for EU customers; do you support region pinning and KMS?
01:06 Marcus Chen: yes, hosted supports region selection for storage and inference regionally and we integrate with KMS for envelope encryption of customer keys. for enterprise private options you can get customer-managed KMS and VPC peering.
01:20 Daniel Ruiz: ok good. show us the rerank flow.
01:24 Marcus Chen: sure. so typical flow: you use elastic for candidate generation, pass top N candidates to Redwood's rerank endpoint as the context + query, we run an embeddings similarity + cross-encoder style reranker and return a re-ordered list with scores. I'll share the postman/snippet after the call.
01:40 Marcus Chen: demo time — i'm switching to the console. note: the console shows token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency and a rerank trace.
02:05 Marcus Chen: here i'm calling the embeddings endpoint — sending 3 documents, getting back 1536-d vectors (in this example we used a curie-like open model). transcript note: some model names get munged in auto-transcribe e.g., 'curie' may be read as 'curry' — ignore transcription artifacts.
02:28 Speaker 1: (background) mm-hmm
02:33 Marcus Chen: next i call the rerank endpoint, payload includes query, candidate ids, and the text snippets. you can include metadata tokens to bias results. response includes confidence and token-level timing.
02:48 Priya Kumar: what's the P95 latency for rerank with 10 candidates?
02:51 Marcus Chen: on hosted default profile P95 is around 120-200ms for a 10-candidate rerank depending on model and sequence lengths. with our compact quantized models you can see P95 ~80-120ms but with slightly less semantic nuance.
03:10 Daniel Ruiz: what's the unit cost and how do we control it?
03:13 Lena Park: cost levers are batching, caching, and model selection. you can cache embeddings or prefixes, do continuous batching for background queries, or pick a cheaper embedding model for high volume. we'll send a cost-runbook after this.
03:25 Maya Lopez: do you store the text we send for reranking? we have strict retention policies.
03:29 Marcus Chen: by default hosted keeps short logs for debugging but you can opt-out of retention; for enterprise we have no-retain options and Private deployments where data never leaves your VPC. also SOC2 and ISO attestation available.
03:45 Speaker 2: oh okay
04:00 Marcus Chen: i'll show a quick relevance before/after for a small dataset. here is a search for "renewal process api" — baseline elastic results show fuzzy matches; after embeddings+rerank we surface more semantically relevant docs.
04:18 Daniel Ruiz: that looks promising. do you do negative sampling or active learning for reranker tuning?
04:22 Marcus Chen: yes we have an evals/optimize toolkit — Redwood Optimize — that ingests labeled pairs, runs regressions, and suggests model + quantization choices. it can also generate prompts to surface failures.
04:40 Priya Kumar: what about throughput? some of our endpoints need sustained 400 qps.
04:45 Marcus Chen: hosted can autoscale but sustained very-high throughput is usually a Dedicated commitment — dedicated GPU pools with predictable throughput and burst policies. we can run a sizing exercise; for 400 qps rerank you'd likely need reserved capacity.
04:58 Lena Park: note that the decision often comes down to predictable latency at scale and cost. many teams start hosted for POC and move to dedicated when they need guaranteed throughput.
05:12 Maya Lopez: one of our worries is query latency tail. do you support canary deployments for reranker models?
05:17 Marcus Chen: yes, the console supports rollouts: canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a cheaper model if the canary exceeds latency SLOs. we also expose traces so you can correlate slow requests.
05:32 Priya Kumar: any partners or competitors you see customers moving from?
05:36 Lena Park: commonly Elastic customers experiment with Algolia or OpenSearch with their own ML; we've seen migrations when teams want unified inference tools plus observability.
05:46 Daniel Ruiz: how hard is integration — do we need to change our query pipeline?
05:50 Marcus Chen: minimal. pattern is: 1) candidate gen in elastic (no change), 2) call Redwood rerank with top N ids and snippets, 3) render re-ranked docs. SDKs have helpers to batch candidates and manage cache keys.
06:10 Marcus Chen: small gotcha: embedding dimension mismatch if you use different models for index vs rerank; we recommend standardizing on the same embedding family or using a mapping during POC.
06:28 Priya Kumar: you mentioned region pinning earlier — how about data residency for EU customers?
06:32 Marcus Chen: hosted supports selecting eu-central and eu-west regions; for strict residency we recommend Private with customer-managed storage.
06:42 Maya Lopez: are there sample benchmarks we can run?
06:45 Marcus Chen: yes — we typically run a 5k-query rerank benchmark: measure throughput, P50/P95 latency, and per-req token cost. i'll run this against a snapshot if you share the anonymized logs.
06:58 Priya Kumar: okay sounds good. what about SAML/SSO and RBAC?
07:02 Lena Park: enterprise includes SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM provisioning, and granular RBAC. we'll attach the security pack and SOC2 report in the follow-up.
07:15 Daniel Ruiz: we have another question on model updates — how are model rollouts handled?
07:20 Marcus Chen: models are versioned; you can pin routes to model versions and do canary rollout. Optimize will flag quality regressions against baseline prompt sets and we can auto rollback.
07:34 (crosstalk)
07:40 Marcus Chen: showing the console metrics — here's per-route latency and per-token cost for the rerank call, and an A/B test result where reranker improved MRR by ~9% on a sample set. note that's illustrative not Sonora's numbers.
08:02 Maya Lopez: if we want to POC, timeline wise what do you suggest?
08:06 Lena Park: typical POC is 4-6 weeks: week 0 intake and data handoff, week 1-2 benchmark and tuning, week 3 pilot integration, week 4 results and decision.
08:18 Priya Kumar: who are the stakeholders we should involve?
08:21 Lena Park: product manager for relevance, search infra, security/compliance, and an exec sponsor to sign off on commit if dedicated.
08:28 Daniel Ruiz: budget question — can you estimate run-rate for 1M rerank calls per month?
08:34 Lena Park: we'll provide an estimate in the pricing deck; factors are embedding model, rerank model, and caching. approximate ballpark given your mix is included in the follow-up.
08:46 Marcus Chen: quick note on engineering integration: we have a lightweight SDK in python and node, with examples for elastic candidate pipeline. sample code will be in the follow-up repo link.
09:02 Priya Kumar: are there existing customers in our vertical?
09:05 Lena Park: yes a couple of vertical search providers and SaaS products run similar setups — i'm happy to connect references after NDA if needed.
09:14 (pause)
09:20 Daniel Ruiz: let's talk about evaluations — do you surface qualitative failure cases?
09:24 Marcus Chen: Optimize supports test sets, A/B metrics, and a failure dashboard with examples; it can suggest model + quantization combos to reduce cost while maintaining quality.
09:36 Priya Kumar: fine, i think we have enough to continue. couple of security asks: SOC2 report, encryption at rest details, and proof of KMS integration.
09:46 Lena Park: we'll send the security one-pager and SOC2 attestation link.
09:50 Marcus Chen: i'll add the benchmark run to action items once maya provides logs.
10:00 Maya Lopez: i'll gather logs and ping you in slack, i'll anonymize them first.
10:05 Lena Park: great. recap of next steps: we'll send pricing + security docs, marcus will run the 5k benchmark, maya will provide logs, and we schedule POC kickoff pending results.
10:18 Priya Kumar: thanks everyone. last question: any concerns about vendor lock-in?
10:22 Marcus Chen: we design for portability — standard embeddings, export formats, and ability to pin model version or migrate to Dedicated/Private.
10:32 Lena Park: thanks again, we'll follow up by EOD with deck and next steps.
10:38 (meeting ends)
